title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #1
body: Ask which school and the city sorts itself instantly. Dubai College, JESS, Repton is one world. GEMS Wellington is comfortable. DPS and Our Own is a completely different life and both sides know it. It's a sealed deal if they say the school once, flatly, and clearly assume you already know what that means.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #2
body: Ask what they drive at seventeen and watch. A Nissan Patrol is the Dubai answer and it is always white. A G-Wagon at that age means the father did not buy it as a lesson. Anyone driving a Corolla in that school car park is being taught something deliberate. It's a sealed deal if the car is registered in a company's name.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #3
body: Watch the accent, because Dubai kids have one that exists nowhere else. Not British, not American, not desi, formed entirely in an international school by twelve nationalities. Their parents' accent is completely different and nobody in that house finds this strange. It's a sealed deal if they say "innit" and "like literally" in the same sentence and mean both.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #4
body: Ask about going back, because that word is doing a lot of work. Their passport says Pakistan. They've been four times. They call it home because their parents do, and they cannot name three roads in the city they're from. It's a sealed deal if a grandparent's house is the only address there they could actually find.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #5
body: Watch the weekend. Kite Beach in the morning, Dubai Mall in the afternoon because everything is in Dubai Mall, then a brunch someone's older sibling got them into. In summer nobody goes outside at all between June and September. It's a sealed deal if they've genuinely never taken a bus in this city and would not know where to start.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #6
body: Ask about Global Village and watch the split. Some families go every year and it's a whole tradition. Others haven't been since 2016 and say so slightly apologetically. Neither is wrong, but it tells you exactly which Dubai that family lives in. It's a sealed deal if a teenager says "that's more of a Karama thing" and hears themselves say it.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #7
body: Ask what happens after school and it's already decided. UK if the family is settled, Canada if they're hedging, and a handful stay for a business degree here and take over something. Nobody in this tier is considering a Pakistani university and nobody says that out loud. It's a sealed deal if the university was chosen partly because a cousin is already in that city.

title: How to (Accidentally) Meet the Rich Kids of Dubai. Tip #8
body: Watch how they talk to the staff at a restaurant, because in this city it's the sharpest tell there is. The kids raised properly say please to everyone. The ones who weren't don't look up. Same school, same car, completely different family. It's a sealed deal if a seventeen-year-old knows the name of the man who has parked their car for three years.
